name: Sky Woman (Haudenosaunee creation figure; names vary by nation)

domain_history.domain: primordial creator figure — falls from the sky world to a water-covered earth; animals dive to retrieve soil placed on Turtle's back (Turtle Island); gives birth to a daughter whose own pregnancy produces the Twins

notes: Names vary genuinely by nation, not interchangeably: Ataensic/Ataentsic/Atahensic (Huron form); Iagentci/Awenhai (Seneca); Iotsitsisonh/Atsiʼtsiaka:ion (Mohawk); Awenhai (Cayuga). "Sky Woman" is a descriptive English title, not a proper name in any one language. Primary scholarly anchor: J.N.B. Hewitt (Tuscarora ethnologist/linguist), Iroquoian Cosmology, Smithsonian Bureau of American Ethnology, Part 1 (1903) and Part 2 (1928) — records three separate versions of the creation narrative (Onondaga, Seneca, Mohawk) as literal translations, deliberately not flattened into one composite myth.
